correctness.rationale: Scaling off-diagonal entries to -1 gives eigenvalues r-2,r+1,r+1 and equal column p-norms; diagonal matrices give quotient 1. On (0,2) the logarithmic derivative has the sign of 1-r-r^(p-1), with its unique zero in (0,1). Negative parameters in [-1,0] give at most the value at zero; those below -1 and parameters at least 2 give values below 1 by comparison with |r|^3. At r=1/2 the columns are orthogonal and their norms strictly decrease from p=2, giving a value above 1 for p>2. This proves global uniqueness up to scale. Substitution of r^p=r(1-r) yields B_p and B_3=phi, with phi^3>4. The three-coordinate embedding proves only a lower bound on the full real constant. At p=2 the sharp bound follows by Cauchy–Binet and the Gram determinant inequality, with infinite sequences handled by finite truncation. At infinity, multiaffinity reduces every minor bound to a sign matrix; divisibility by 4, the Euclidean Hadamard bound below 8, and the attaining sign matrix prove the sharp value 4. Thus the sharp-real-endpoint interpolation prediction fails, without conflicting with complex interpolation. The frozen script was inspected, not executed; its sampled exponents do not certify the continuum optimum.
